Control: Strong password policy enforced (length >= 12, complexity, rotation)
MFA enabled for privileged accounts
Default vendor accounts disabled or credentials changed
Account lockout works after repeated failed logins
Least privilege applied across all database roles
RBAC used instead of direct permission grants
Formal onboarding/offboarding for access provisioning
Periodic user access reviews; inactive accounts deactivated
Admin rights restricted and reviewed quarterly
No shared administrative accounts
Administrative actions logged and reviewed regularly
Sensitive columns/tables encrypted (AES-256 or equivalent)
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled
Encryption keys stored in a Key Management System
SSL/TLS 1.2+ for client and inter-server connections
Secure drivers and trusted-authority certificates used
Key lifecycle policy (generation, storage, rotation, destruction)
Key access limited to authorized security personnel
Database in a segregated network zone (DMZ/Internal LAN)
Firewall default-deny with explicit allow rules
Inbound/outbound limited to approved IPs and ports
IDS/IPS or SIEM integration for real-time analysis
Regular vulnerability scans of database servers reviewed
Detailed auditing enabled (logins, DDL/DML, privilege changes)
Logs retained at least 90 days in a secure central location
Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) detects abnormal behavior
Quarterly log reviews with documented follow-up
Backups automated, encrypted and stored offsite/cloud
Restoration tested quarterly
Retention aligned with BCP and compliance requirements
Backup and DR procedures documented
Database servers in physically secured environments
Patches applied per patch management policy
Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing done annually
DLP and Database Firewall implemented
Data classification policy and sensitivity labelling
Security awareness training for admins and users
